To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) stress, shift duty, working hours, and body mass index were associated with eating behavior; (2) stress was positively associated with all eating styles, and negatively associated with healthy eating; (3) shift work was positively associated with emotional and restrained eating, and negatively associated to external eating; and (4) the association between stress and shift duty and eating styles were more significant under a restraint eating behavior.
